In this work, we use bipartite OTOC, a particular form of OTOC, to study information scrambling in the atom–field interaction models and the model of the Ising spin chain interacting with a tilted magnetic field. This is done considering the effects of open quantum systems. A relationship between information scrambling, using bipartite OTOC, and irreversibility, using entropy production, is probed under unitary dynamics. The equivalence of bipartite OTOC with operator entanglement is explicitly shown for the Ising model.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/ad77ee\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 9, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1088/1367-2630/13/7/073038\", \"title\": [\"Redundant information from thermal illumination: quantum Darwinism in scattered photons\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/13/7/073038\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2011, 7, 27]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-0-387-25554-5_9\", \"title\": [\"Temporal Distinguishability of a Multi-Photon State\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-25554-5_9\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2007]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.26421/qic14.1-2-2\", \"title\": [\"Comparisons between quantum state distinguishability measures\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>We provide a compendium of inequalities between several quantum state distinguishability measures. For each measure these inequalities consist of the sharpest possible upper and lower bounds in terms of another measure. Some of these inequalities are already known, but new or more general proofs are given, whereas other inequalities are new. We also supply cases of equality to show that all inequalities are indeed the sharpest possible.</jats:p>\", \"U…
